title.en: What Your Kidneys Sift Out Each Day

text.zh: 从背后看，腰的上方藏着两个拳头大的器官。它们每天要把你全身的血反复过滤几十遍。
text.en: Seen from behind, two fist-sized organs sit just above the waist. Every day they filter the whole of your blood over and over.

text.zh: 这就是肾。它们不在腰眼上，而是更靠上、贴着后腹壁，被最后两根肋骨护着。
text.en: These are the kidneys. They sit higher than most people think, pressed against the back wall of the abdomen and shielded by the last two ribs.

text.zh: 血从肾动脉直接进来。这两根动脉很短很粗，直接从主动脉分出——原料必须又快又足。
text.en: Blood arrives through the renal arteries, short and thick and branching straight off the aorta: the supply must be both fast and generous.

text.zh: 过滤发生在外圈的肾皮质。血浆在这里被整批挤出血管，好东西随后再一点点收回去。
text.en: Filtering happens in the outer shell, the renal cortex. Plasma is squeezed wholesale out of the vessels here, and the useful parts are reclaimed afterwards.

text.zh: 再往里是一个个尖端朝内的肾锥体。液体穿过它们时被反复浓缩，越走越少、越走越浓。
text.en: Deeper in stand the renal pyramids, their tips pointing inward. Fluid passing through them is concentrated again and again — less in volume, stronger in content.

text.zh: 所有锥体的出口汇进肾盂，像漏斗一样收成一股，交给下一段管道。
text.en: The outlets of every pyramid drain into the renal pelvis, which gathers them into a single stream like a funnel and hands it on.

text.zh: 输尿管把液体一路送到骨盆。它不是靠重力，而是靠管壁一波波蠕动往下挤——躺着也照样走。
text.en: The ureters carry the fluid down to the pelvis. Not by gravity but by waves of muscular squeezing along the wall — so it keeps moving even lying down.

text.zh: 终点是膀胱。它空着时壁很厚、皱成一团，装满时能撑得又薄又大，像个可折叠的口袋。
text.en: The journey ends at the bladder. Empty, its wall is thick and crumpled; full, it stretches thin and wide — a pocket that folds away when unused.

text.zh: 所以尿不是「废水」，而是筛剩下的那一点。真正的工作，是把该留的都留了下来。
text.en: So urine is not simply waste water but the small remainder after sifting. The real work was keeping everything worth keeping.
